note: One word with a size parameter: 224, 256, 384, 512 (the default, as in CyberChef), 512/224, 512/256. Returns raw bytes (chain hex:encode). CyberChef's Rounds parameter is not supported: only the FIPS 180-4 round counts exist.
No parameters. Returns raw bytes (chain hex:encode).
No parameters. Returns raw bytes (chain hex:encode).
One word with a size parameter in bits: 224, 256, 384, 512 (the default, as in CyberChef). Returns raw bytes (chain hex:encode).
One word with a size parameter in bits: 224, 256, 384, 512 (the default, as in CyberChef), with the original Keccak padding (not SHA-3).

The output length is in bytes (1 to 65536, default 64), where CyberChef's Size is in bits (default 512, so the default is the same 64 bytes; the bits are a multiple of 8 in Forge). The variant is 128 or 256, the security strength in bits, as in CyberChef's Capacity (default 256 in both).

The output size is in bytes (16, 20, 32, 48 or 64, default 64), where CyberChef's Size is in bits (128, 160, 256, 384, 512, default 512). The key is an optional key of up to 64 bytes in any of the key encodings.
The output size is in bytes (16, 20 or 32, default 32), where CyberChef's Size is in bits (128, 160, 256, default 256). The key is an optional key of up to 32 bytes in any of the key encodings.
The output length is in bytes (1 to 65536, default 32, the BLAKE3 specification's default output; CyberChef's default is 16). The key is an optional 32-byte key, as in CyberChef.

Hash choice: md2, md4, md5, sha0, sha1, sha224, sha256 (the default; CyberChef's first choice, and so its default, is MD2), sha384, sha512, sha512/224, sha512/256, ripemd128, ripemd160, ripemd256, ripemd320, has160, whirlpool and snefru, which are every CyberChef choice except Whirlpool-0 and Whirlpool-T (Forge does not implement those variants of Whirlpool). The four SHA-3 sizes (sha3-224, sha3-256, sha3-384, sha3-512) are extra: CyberChef's HMAC has no SHA-3. snefru is Snefru with a 128-bit output and 8 passes, as CyberChef uses. The key is a key param in any of the key encodings (utf8, hex, latin1 or base64; CyberChef also offers Decimal, which Forge does not), empty by default. The output is the raw MAC bytes (chain hex:encode), where CyberChef shows hex text. Blake2 and BLAKE3 keyed modes are their own words.
